findings.problem: Exported LIMITS is declared `as const` (compile-time only) and is not Object.freeze'd, so the runtime object is mutable by any code in the same module root. Observed: after `LIMITS.maxTextChars = 999999`, validateStaticDelivery accepted a 5000-char text that it had rejected with `text_too_long` moments earlier (raw/09-mutability-and-types.txt).
findings.impact: In-process only, and self-inflicted: no untrusted wire input reaches LIMITS (validators only read it), defaults enforce correctly, and a second module root remained unaffected, so AC4 cross-root independence still holds. It is a defense-in-depth gap for a trust-boundary library, not a bypass reachable from a protocol message.
findings.requiredFix: Non-blocking for S0. Wrap the LIMITS object literal in Object.freeze() (and optionally METHODS/KNOWN_CAPABILITIES/RECEIPT_LEVELS) so documented limits cannot be weakened at runtime. Defer to S1 if the owner prefers zero further S0 churn.
findings.acLink: AC3 (concrete enforced limits) — hardening only; AC3 gate itself passes

findings.problem: validateJobCreate explicitly discards the caller clock (`void nowMs`), so a once-schedule with a past atUtc (e.g. 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z) validates successfully. Observed as case sched.once.past.OBSERVED-ACCEPTED in raw/07-consumer-probe.txt.
findings.impact: None for S0. AC3 requires format/calendar validation and bounded expiry/notAfter (all enforced and verified); it explicitly forbids implementing scheduling in this lane. Past-vs-future schedule semantics belong to the S1 scheduler contract.
findings.requiredFix: No S0 action. Record as an explicit S1 scheduler requirement so a past-dated once job has defined behavior (reject vs immediate-fire vs skip) when scheduling lands.
